basis: Meningeal tumour of the anterior visual pathway; visual impairment from a CNS lesion does not alone establish ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: the record does not establish direct eye or optic-nerve damage in at least about 30%; optic-tract dysfunction is neurologic.

basis: Named neurodevelopmental syndrome with eye and heart anomalies, each frequent (30-79%); congenital urinary tract dysfunction includes vesicoureteral reflux in 3/10.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: heart anomalies are an explicitly named syndrome component; abnormal heart morphology is frequent, with VSD in 4/10.
decisions.ocular: primary: eye anomalies are an explicitly named syndrome component and frequent (30-79%), including structural ocular and optic-nerve abnormalities.

basis: The definition describes congenital pancreatic hyperinsulinism; persistent hypoglycemic neurodevelopmental injury affects roughly 30-50% of congenital cases.

decisions.neurologic: involved: congenital hyperinsulinism, as defined here, causes lasting neurodevelopmental injury in roughly 30-50%, beyond transient hypoglycemic symptoms.

basis: Hair defects, developmental impairment and joint laxity define the syndrome; valve regurgitation reported in 1/1 supports cardiac involvement. Microdontia omitted at cap; sample is tiny.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: joint laxity is part of the syndrome's explicit synonym; joint hypermobility and multiple skeletal abnormalities support this defining component.

basis: Fanconi marrow-failure syndrome; microcephaly 3/7 does not establish neurologic dysfunction. Anal atresia 2/7 is below 30%; pigment spots are nondamaging and cancers are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly in 3/7 establishes small head size, without documented brain dysfunction; subsequent brain tumours are separate diseases.

basis: Immune dysregulation with defining inflammatory skin disease; pneumonitis/bronchiolitis and enterocolitis each occur in 2/2. Ocular lesions in 1/2 omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: persistent blistering inflammatory skin disease is a defining clinical feature of APLAID, beyond transient erythema.

basis: Intellectual disability and hypogonadism define the syndrome. Microtia is frequent (80-99%), but hearing loss or other functional ear damage is not established.

decisions.otologic: none: microtia in 80-99% is external-ear dysmorphism; the supplied evidence does not establish associated hearing loss or functional damage.

basis: Blood and marrow AML; direct leukemic skin infiltration occurs in approximately 30-50% of reported t(8;16) cases, with higher frequencies in childhood presentations.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: leukemia cutis is characteristic of this cytogenetic subtype, reported in approximately 30-50%; it represents direct tumour infiltration.

basis: Cobalamin metabolic disorder with defining neurodevelopmental impairment; intellectual disability is an explicit parent and synonym, with developmental delay in 12/14 and seizures in 9/14.

decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is an explicit parent and synonym; developmental delay in 12/14 and seizures in 9/14 support a core neurodevelopmental phenotype.

basis: Arthrogryposis, femoral necrosis and upgaze palsy define the syndrome; pulmonary valve stenosis and pyloric stenosis each occur in 2/3. Asthma is a separately diagnosed disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: asthma in 3/3 is a separately diagnosed associated disease; no intrinsic pulmonary malformation or other direct syndrome-related lung injury is established.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: congenital pyloric stenosis in 2/3 directly impairs gastrointestinal function and is a structural component of the syndrome.
